provenance: OC-022: first graded-pack benchmark over two physically-distinct measured datasets. Geometry, sampling, limits and cost blocks match the OC-020 family (racetrack, 0.3 m straight half-length, 0.2 m bend radius, 0.9 T bore target, util limit 0.8); sampling adds a 0.85-fraction turn index after a refined plan found an interior minimum at ~0.85N that the coarse plan missed (3.9% shortfall in calibration). Regions split turns_along_normal at the radial midpoint: inner half sees the higher field, outer half the lower. Each region takes base or hts-shanghai. Both specs bind real embedded measured datasets from the same Robinson instrument/criterion: base is robinson-superpower-ap-v3 (SuperPower AP 12 mm tape, 1 mm bridge, csv_sha256 889cc2cf8b91b822cbc6cceb7388e5d8afcb8a8911bb20ab175e50c7e6dc0354, monotonicity_tolerance 0.001, low_field_clamp_t 1.001); hts-shanghai is robinson-shanghai-hflt-v3 (Shanghai Superconductor HFLT 4 mm tape, 0.5 mm bridge, csv_sha256 d53fbab65426c2d2f00ddd19ebe0470b1f73fb8a3e64b23b8f7ae871ec29c4a3, low_field_clamp_t 1.001). The hts-shanghai binding declares monotonicity_tolerance 0.025, justified against the dataset audit: 4 of 1289 nominal (T, angle) field-sweep pairs show measured Ic increasing between 7 and 8 T, worst +2.32% — plausibly IV-fit noise at the instrument field limit, but a real non-monotonicity the stricter 0.002 tolerance rejects, sending every lower-bound point to UNSUPPORTED per contract A8. The base binding keeps 0.001. Prices are invented placeholders (base 30 USD/m, hts-shanghai 34 USD/m — a ~13% premium for the tape with the stronger measured high-field response), not vendor quotes. Per-width measured capacity is compared at the case-level 12 mm tape width; the 4 mm product-width difference is a stated limitation, not modeled.
